{{ block title }} Instructions {{ endblock }} {{ block content }}

In this experiment there are two kinds of players: "Player A" and "Player B". Both work for 5 minutes on a real-effort task. As a player, you have to complete a counting task, where you have to count how many “ones” there are in a grid full of zeros and ones. You receive a piece rate payment for each correctly solved puzzle.

{{ if player.participant.control }} Player A receives for each correctly solved puzzle a piece rate of 8 pence. In addition, Player A can also extract some part of the performance pay of a Player B who is matched with him/her.
This is described in more detail below.
By contrast, each Player B competes with another Player B. Player B's compensation depends on the outcome of a tournament against the other Player B.
If Player B wins the tournament he/she receives a piece rate of 8 pence for each correctly solved puzzle.
If he/she loses the tournament, she earns nothing (0 pence).
If there is a tie, a random draw decides about the winner.


In addition to the number of correctly solved puzzles, payment of Player B also depends on a decision of Player A: Each Player B is matched with one Player A. Before the players start working, Player A can define how much of Player B’s real-effort performance he/she wants to extract. To do this, he/she has to define the percentage of real-effort extraction (0-100% in increments of 10 percent), he/she is willing to take from Player B. Both players know that at the end of the real-effort task, Player A receives the percentage of Player B's real-effort performance as defined by Player A before. This percentage is subtracted from Player B's performance. All this is known to both players from the beginning. {{ else }} Player A competes with another Player A, and Player B competes with another Player B. Each Player A is matched with a Player B. Player A's compensation depends on the outcome of a tournament against the other Player A, and Player B's compensation depends on the outcome of a tournament against the other Player B.
If Player A wins the tournament, he/she receives a piece rate of 16 pence for each correctly solved puzzle.
If Player B wins the tournament, he/she receives a piece rate of 8 pence for each correctly solved puzzle.
If a Player loses the tournament, he/she earns nothing (0 pence).
If there is a tie, a random draw decides about the winner.


In addition to the number of correctly solved puzzles, payment also depends on a decision of Player A: Each Player B is matched with one Player A. Before the players start working, Player A can define how much of Player B’s real-effort performance he/she wants to extract. To do this, he/she has to define the percentage of real-effort extraction (0-100% in increments of 10 percent), he/she is willing to take from Player B. Both players know that at the end of the real-effort task, Player A receives the percentage of Player B's real-effort performance as defined by Player A before. This percentage is subtracted from Player B's performance. All this is known to both players from the beginning. {{ endif }}
Player B will be informed about the percentage player A decided to extract before starting with the real-effort task.

{{ if player.participant.is_senior }} You have been assigned the role of Player A! {{ else }} You have been assigned the role of Player B! {{ endif }}
